newsitem.title: USA: Corn harvest begins in southern Indiana.
newsitem.headline: Corn harvest begins in southern Indiana.

text.p: Corn harvest was underway in the southern tip of Indiana during the week ended Sunday, according to the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service weekly crop report.
Corn was nine percent mature, behind the 21 percent five-year average. The crop was rated five percent very poor, 17 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 36 percent good and five percent excellent.
A few soybean fields had been harvested but most of the crop was still a few weeks from maturity. Seven percent had begun shedding leaves compared with average of 20 percent.
Soybeans were rated six percent very poor, 19 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 31 percent good and four percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated 38 percent very short, 44 percent short, 17 percent adequate and one percent surplus.
Pasture and range conditions were rated 18 percent very poor, 34 percent poor, 35 percent fair, 12 percent good and one percent excellent.
